blocks.text: In Naimisha forest, the sages gather and ask: tell us the tale of the Bharatas. Sauti bows, and the fire leans in to listen.
King Janamejaya feeds serpents to the flames to avenge his father. Astika steps forward: when does justice become vengeance?
Shantanu loves the river herself. Seven sons she returns to the waters; the eighth she leaves behind — Devavrata.
For his father's desire, Devavrata renounces crown and child. The gods rain flowers and name him Bhishma — the terrible oath.
A blind prince, a pale prince, a wise minister's son. The throne of Hastinapura learns to fear its own bloodline.
A hundred Kauravas. Five Pandavas, god-born. And on the river, a basket carries away Karna — the son no one claimed.
Under Drona, Arjuna becomes peerless. Ekalavya pays his fee with his thumb. Excellence, too, has a price.
A palace of lacquer, built to burn. Warned by Vidura, the Pandavas vanish through the earth while the fire tells its lie.
In the dark forest, hunger has a name. Bhima kills Hidimba, spares love — and a new lineage begins.
The bow bends for a Brahmin youth. Draupadi's garland chooses Arjuna — and, by a mother's word, binds five brothers.
Hastinapura cannot hold both houses. The Pandavas are given a wasteland — and turn exile into a plan.
Fire clears Khandava; a white city rises. Every victory contains a wound — and every ending, a seed.
